topics.topic: StoreHistory identity creation and restore semantics
questions: What constitutes the identity of the StoreHistory entity, who mints it, and what happens to that identity when a backup is restored as a new history?
What identifies StoreHistory, who mints that identity, and does restoring a backup preserve the backed-up StoreHistory identity or mint a new identity for the new history?
Who creates the StoreHistory entity for a new store and for a restored store, what fact distinguishes the new history from the history captured by the backup, and from what is that identity minted?

quotes:
The facts listed under a model are all its facts, and the facts a create
request supplies are named with it (State 0, "Carried to later states"); a fact
that may be absent says so in domain words ("when given").

Substitution: a store holds one history; a second record with equal facts
would be a second history of one store, which R0-89 does not have.
Continuity: the history stays the same while its last sequence number moves
with every entry and its migration closure appears; a restore after a loss
begins a new history, from the backup's facts (R0-89).

Durable, exactly one per store, made with the store and changed only inside
the transaction of an audit append or of the import.

None. No caller reads it as such: the audit view, the backup record (A18) and
the import's refusal (R0-79) read its facts.
judgement.why: StoreHistory is the entity corresponding to one store history, is made with that store without a separately minted identifier, and a restore begins a new entity from the backup's facts.

topics.topic: Handling absent, other, and unsupported Object kinds
questions: For an object not described by apartment, house or commercial, must Registry record `other`, may it leave kind absent, or are absence and `other` distinct facts chosen by the owner?
When a create or correction supplies a kind outside the closed vocabulary, must Registry refuse it, store `other`, or treat the kind as absent?

quotes:
Facts: address (required at creation, R0-45); kind, one of a closed vocabulary
the specification declares ("Declared vocabularies"), optional at creation; the
declared characteristics, each optional at creation and in every correction:

- Object kind: `apartment`, `house`, `commercial` (premises for a business),
  `other` (R0-38; owner, 2026-11-11; round 1 T10). `other` keeps the kind
  optional in meaning as in form: an object no member describes is never
  refused.

A project has exactly one object: its address, its kind and the technical
characteristics the specification declares. The address moves from the project
to the object; `context` keeps answering `address`, read from the object
(R0-04). Rooms stay on the project (R0-10). Options (b), an object carrying
several projects with the rooms on it, and (c), no separate object, were
declined.
judgement.divergence: For an object outside the three specific categories, one implementation records `other` while another leaves kind absent; the owner and trusted services reading the project card observe different Object facts.
judgement.why: The closed set excludes an unsupported literal, but the texts do not decide whether an unclassified object's stored fact is `other` or absent.

witness.initial: The owner is creating a project for an object not described by `apartment`, `house`, or `commercial`.
events: The owner creates the project with its required address and describes the object as a warehouse.
The owner or a trusted service reads the resulting project card.
outcomes: The embedded Object carries no kind.

topics.topic: Initial audit sequence number for a restored StoreHistory
questions: When restoration creates a new history, is its initial last sequence number 0 because that history has written no entries, or the number inherited from the backup?

When a restore begins a new history from a backup recording sequence N, is that new history's initial last audit sequence number N even though the new history has written no entry, or is it 0 until the new history writes one?

quotes:
- the last audit sequence number the history ever wrote: 0 for a history
  that wrote none, then moved to each new entry's number in that entry's
  transaction; never lowered, also when old entries are erased (R0-66); a
  store restored from a backup begins its history from the number that
  backup records (R0-89; State 2 A18);
judgement.why: The restore-specific clause explicitly makes the backed-up number, rather than 0, the restored history's initial value.

topics.topic: Whether Object kind and Customer language are enums or vocabularies
questions: Which closed model kind does each newly declared Object kind and Customer language set have: `enum` or `vocabulary`?
Must Object kind become a `kind: enum` named type used by runtime fields, or a read-only `kind: vocabulary` spec-data model?
Must Customer language become a `kind: enum` named type used by runtime fields, or a read-only `kind: vocabulary` spec-data model?

quotes:
These are closed sets the specification declares; in State 6 they become
`kind: enum` or `kind: vocabulary` models without identity (SPEC_STANDARD §5).
judgement.why: Choosing the formal model kind used by runtime fields or read-only specification data is a State 6 schema and type decision.

topics.topic: Organization of StoreHistory facts by independent change axes
questions: The passage must split or otherwise reorganize these facts according to their change axes: the audit sequence changes on audit appends, while MigrationClosure appears once for the independent reason that an import succeeded.

topics.topic: Whether a restored StoreHistory inherits MigrationClosure
questions: Can a restored StoreHistory begin with MigrationClosure already present from a post-import backup, or must every restored history begin without it and record a closure only after it begins?

quotes: begun (store made new, or restored) -> number moves -> closure recorded (once)

Continuity: the history stays the same while its last sequence number moves
with every entry and its migration closure appears; a restore after a loss
begins a new history, from the backup's facts (R0-89).
judgement.divergence: The lifecycle orders closure recording after every restored history begins, while restoration from a post-import backup begins the new history with the backed-up closure already present; the owner attempting another import observes acceptance versus refusal.
judgement.why: The linear lifecycle requires a restored history to reach closure only after it begins, but the identity evidence says that the restored history begins from all backup facts, which can already include the closure.

witness.initial: Production has completed the import, recorded its MigrationClosure, and made a backup containing that fact.
events: The owner puts the post-import backup in its place outside Registry.
Registry starts on the restored store.
The owner attempts the import again.
outcomes: Following the lifecycle sequence, the restored history begins before any closure is recorded in it, so the import can be accepted.
Following restoration from the backup's facts, the restored history begins with MigrationClosure present, so the import is refused.
basis:
Registry makes daily encrypted backups and checks each one (State 2). It has
no restore operation: when the store is lost, the owner puts a backup in its
place on the host, outside Registry (Explicit exclusions), and Registry
starts on it as on any store.
